name: Metropolis Healthcare Ltd
title: Metropolis Healthcare Ltd - 542650 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 revenue +16% and H1 EBITDA margin 26.2% (+190 bps) with no price hike; capacity held at 750 towns and capex flat at INR65-70 cr, but FY27 margin guide was narrowed to 120-170 bps versus prior 100-150 bps and a calibrated price hike is planned for Q4.

summary.headline: Metropolis Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR497 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 180 bps to 27.2%, with no price increase in the period.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 16% year-on-year to INR497 crore, ahead of guidance, driven by 10% patient volume and 11% test volume growth. EBITDA rose 24% to INR135 crore (27.2% margin, up 180 bps) and PAT rose 43% to INR75 crore (15.2% margin, up 290 bps). H1 FY27 revenue grew 16.2% with EBITDA margin at 26.2% (up 190 bps), all achieved without a price increase. Management flagged a calibrated B2C price revision for Q4 FY27 or early FY28, and an interim dividend of INR1 per share was declared.

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 17% in Q2 and H1, with patient volume up 13.5% and test volume up 11%; existing centres delivered 10% same-store growth. Company added 116 collection centres in Q2 and 700 net over 24 months.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15% in Q2, with patient volume up 7% and test volume up 11%. B2B partner network crossed 9,000; partner churn is now low single-digit versus close to double-digit earlier.

segments.name: Specialty
segments.commentary: Contributed 40% of Q2 revenue and grew about 20% YoY; 43 specialty and super-specialty tests added in H1, with Core's oncology portfolio cross-sold.

segments.name: TruHealth (preventive)
segments.commentary: Contributed 17% of Q2 revenue and grew 20% YoY; radiology-inclusive packages and doctor consults, vitals and ECG add-ons are gaining traction.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Tier 3 and rural centres grew about 20% and now make up 26% of domestic revenue. North contributes about 17% of domestic revenue; Q2 North organic growth was 12% per slide 9, and management said North is the fastest-growing zone organically.

segments.name: Core Diagnostics (acquired 1.5 years ago)
segments.commentary: Was at breakeven at acquisition and now earns near double-digit margins (double-digit in Q2). Management estimates IRR of about 13% so far, rising in H2.

guidance_outlook: H1 FY27 pace (about 16% revenue growth, 180-200 bps margin expansion) expected to continue through H2 FY27, per Q&A.

Management's stated EBITDA margin expansion for FY27 was given as 120-170 bps in the opening remarks and reconfirmed as similar to H1 trends; analyst questioned this versus the earlier upper end of 150 bps.
Medium-term margin expansion of about 125-150 bps in coming years after investments in about 25 mini hubs and retail product expansion.
Centre-to-lab ratio to move from 24:1 toward about 30:1 by end of FY27 and 30:1 to 35:1 over the next 2 years; no new labs planned, only collection-centre additions in existing 750 towns.
Capex in the normal range of INR65-70 crore for FY27, consistent with 4-5% of revenue.
Lab platform transition to complete in Q3 FY27; calibrated B2C price revision being evaluated, with rollout partly in Q4 FY27 and possibly early FY28, varying by micro-market.
capex_capacity: Capex planned at about INR65-70 crore for FY27, in line with the 4-5% of revenue range; no new labs to be added.
Centre-to-lab ratio at 24:1 today, targeted towards 30:1 by end of FY27 and 35:1 over two years; growth via collection centres in existing 750 towns.
Lab platform transition (common test menu, equipment, reagents, TAT, vendor consolidation) to be completed in Q3 FY27.
About 25 mini hubs being expanded; Insta60 60-minute home visit service launched in Mumbai and Chennai, with Bengaluru planned for early November 2026.
Technology roadmap for H2: new CRM platform, dynamic pricing engine, field sales app, enhanced SLIMS integration with hospital portals, and finance process re-engineering.
demand_pricing: No price increase in FY27 so far; last price increase was January 2025. Management is evaluating a calibrated B2C-focused revision, with rollout in Q4 FY27 for part of the business or early FY28; micro-market based on peer benchmarks, market share and brand equity.
Patient volume growth rose from about 7% a year earlier to 10% in Q2 FY27, driven by new Tier 2/3 labs maturing, branded walk-ins and CLM/digital engagement.
CGHS revenue contribution is minimal, so the CGHS rate revision had no impact on growth; growth is volume and mix based.

Government measures: display of rates at centres welcomed (little operational change); NMC clarified remote digital authorisation of lab reports, enabling central pathologist pools for Tier 3 mini labs.
Management said hospital pharma price caps have no bearing on diagnostics; no price cap or parity move seen in the segment. Hospital outsourcing dynamics said to be unchanged for now.
Management declined to comment on market share, saying there is no credible market share data.

qa_highlights.question: Why is tests per patient around 2, and is the mix skewed to specialty or sickness testing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management counts one TruHealth wellness package as one test regardless of its 50-60 parameters, so the 20% TruHealth growth lowers the reported tests-per-patient ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What share do oncology and genomics have in Specialty, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Oncology is a large part of Specialty and predates the Core acquisition; genomics is only 1.5-2 years old. Management expects both to grow faster than company average, with significant genomics acceleration ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin guidance being revised, and what drives margins from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 delivered 180-190 bps and similar trends are expected. Drivers are operating leverage, lab platform transition, productivity and price revision, partly offset by mini-hub and retail investments; medium-term 125-150 bps expansion expected.

qa_highlights.question: Will the B2C price increase be broad-based or restricted?
qa_highlights.answer: The revision is restricted to B2C for now, with micro-market-specific changes; groundwork takes a couple of months and rollout is expected in Q4 or early next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise prices now, and how will unorganized peers respond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited input, logistics, transport and service cost inflation over two years; FY26 was paused because of GST input benefits. It said it cannot comment on peer behaviour.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Core Diagnostics margin and IRR update?
qa_highlights.answer: Core is at double-digit margins versus breakeven at acquisition 1.5 years ago; estimated IRR about 13% in the past year, expected to accelerate in H2.

risks_watch: Price revision timing and extent (Q4 FY27 or early FY28) and whether volumes hold; management says a calibrated increase should have no meaningful volume impact.
Sustainability of 16% growth against a weak monsoon base; growth was partly sporadic seasonal demand.
Investments in mini hubs, retail products and technology (CRM, dynamic pricing, SLIMS) may dilute margin gains.
Hospital-sector pricing and outsourcing dynamics under government pricing measures, which management said are unproven for diagnostics.
Core Diagnostics IRR and margin progress; North expansion and competition from larger peers in Mumbai.
M&A pipeline discipline: management said it passed on deals at 18-20x EBITDA; no major acquisitions planned this year.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and regulatory tailwinds, with specific numbers given throughout. Management was more measured on price revision scope and peer behaviour, and on market share, where it declined to give data.
key_quotes: Importantly, we have delivered the step-up in growth while expanding EBITDA margins by 190 basis points to 26.2% EBITDA margin for the first half, and this is without any price increase so far in the year.
Diagnostics is not merely a price -driven business. It is a fundamental business driven by science, accuracy, service quality and the trust of doctors and patients.
So we did say that the first half of the year was about 16% is good revenue growth and about 180 to 200 bps margin growth. So we expect the similar trend to continue for the rest of the year as well.

adds.what: 116 collection centres added in Q2 FY27 (700 net over 24 months); growth via collection centres in existing 750 towns, no new labs
Insta60 60-minute home visit service: Mumbai and Chennai live, Bengaluru planned early Nov 2026

growth.why: Management expects H1 FY27 pace of about 16% revenue growth to continue through H2 FY27, backed by 116 collection centres added in Q2, 25 mini hubs being expanded, and 10% patient volume growth, though no order-book style contracts were cited and the margin guide is an EBITDA margin figure rather than a revenue target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose 190 bps to 26.2% and management expects a similar trend (180-200 bps) to continue through H2, with a medium-term 125-150 bps expansion guided after mini-hub and retail investments.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 116 collection centres were added in Q2 and growth continues via collection centres in existing 750 towns, with centre-to-lab ratio moving from 24:1 toward 30:1 by end FY27; no new labs planned, so capacity adds are incremental centres rather than plants.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Patient volume grew 10% in Q2 (up from about 7%), test volume 11%, and management expects H1's about 16% revenue pace to continue through H2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at INR65-70 crore for FY27 (4-5% of revenue) with no new labs planned, and utilisation was not disclosed, so no new major capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated H1 trends (180-200 bps margin, about 16% growth) for H2, which is ahead of the 120-170 bps FY27 margin figure cited by the analyst, but no formal guidance raise was made.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Price revision timing and extent, plus investments in mini hubs, retail and technology (CRM, dynamic pricing, SLIMS), could dilute margin gains, and growth is against a weak monsoon base.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Insta60 60-minute home visits launch in Bengaluru in early Nov 2026 after Mumbai and Chennai, and H2 tech roadmap (CRM, dynamic pricing engine, field sales app) is in train, with 43 specialty tests added in H1.

rows.label: Calibrated B2C price revision
rows.why: No price increase since January 2025 and management cites two years of input, logistics and transport cost inflation; the revision is being evaluated and micro-market specific, with rollout partly in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Core Diagnostics margin and IRR build
rows.why: Core moved from breakeven at acquisition to double-digit margins, with estimated IRR about 13% so far, expected to rise in H2.

rows.label: Lab platform transition completion
rows.why: Common test menu, equipment, reagents and vendor consolidation are slated to complete in Q3 FY27, which management links to operating leverage and margin gains.

tone.note: Management was confident on 16% growth, 180-200 bps margin trend and regulatory tailwinds but measured on price revision scope, peer behaviour and market share; analysts pressed on whether the FY27 margin guide (120-170 bps) was being revised versus the earlier 150 bps upper end.
